_datum: BACK-LEFT corner of the main table top, standing at the bench facing it. +x runs right along the main table, +y runs FORWARD toward where you stand. z is not used here - table surfaces are the top face, and height_to_floor_in carries the vertical.
_measured: 2026-07-26, Kyle: main run and return. Unmeasured values are null ON PURPOSE - the twin models only what is measured and reports the rest as absent, because a guessed obstacle is worse than a missing one (the gate would report CLEAR against a fiction).

surfaces.name: main

surfaces.name: return
surfaces.notes: left-side return, forward of the main run; 27.5 + 48.5 = 76 total depth from the back edge

arm._comment: Where the arm's base centre sits on the table, in datum coords, and which way it faces. yaw_deg is the direction the arm points with m1 at 0 deg: 0 = toward the front of the desk (+y), positive counter-clockwise viewed from above (so +90 points along -x, to the left). SAFETY-CRITICAL: switching the twin from its infinite ground plane to the real finite tabletop makes the gate LESS conservative - it will believe there is air past the table edge. A wrong arm position therefore means the gate can call CLEAR over real tabletop. Until x/y/yaw_deg are measured the twin keeps the infinite plane.

_walls_note: height is USABLE HEIGHT ABOVE THE TABLE TOP, not floor to ceiling - the arm can only ever reach what is above the surface it is bolted to. yaw_deg is the direction the wall RUNS: 0 = along +x, 90 = along +y.
